rounds.text: KHFM Hospitality & Facility Mgt. Services Ltd trades at a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.37x on a book value of ₹ 29.3 against a share price of ₹ 40.2 [E2]. The company demonstrates superior capital efficiency compared to its peers, delivering a ROCE of 8.17% which beats the sector benchmark of 6.56% [E9]. Operational momentum is clearly improving as evidenced by quarterly operating margins expanding to 10% in March 2026, representing a two percentage point increase over the year-ago quarter [E22] and triggering positive margin expansion signals on the scanX engine [E56]. Conceded: the company yields no dividends [E4], sits at the absolute bottom of its 52-week range [E5], and features a modest 3-year median return on equity of 6% [E19].

This subpar return profile is further confirmed by official filings flagging a low return on equity of 6.26% over the last three years [E53] alongside flat-to-contracting longer-term operating margins that dropped from 10% to 9% over a three-year period [E21]. Market sentiment aggressively rejects the current valuation as the stock sits entirely at the bottom of its 52-week range, occupying 0% of its high-low span between a 40 low and an 83 high [E5]. Furthermore, shareholders receive zero cash return on their capital, underscored by a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4]. Conceded: the company demonstrates a strong short-term quarterly operating margin expansion of +2 percentage points to 10% in Mar 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E22] and outperforms the sector benchmark on ROCE [E9].

Conceded: official filings flag a low return on equity of 6.26% over the last three years [E53]. However, the bear's focus on longer-term operating margin contraction from 10% to 9% [E21] completely ignores the more relevant inflection point: quarterly operating margins have expanded by +2 percentage points to 10% in Mar 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E22], directly powering a margin expansion screen signal [E56]. The claim that market sentiment aggressively rejects the valuation via the 52-week range sitting at 0% of its high-low span [E5] simply highlights an extreme washout price of ₹ 40.2 [E2] that provides an attractive entry point near absolute support rather than a fundamental impairment. Furthermore, the 0.00% dividend yield [E4] does not mean capital destruction; it reflects earnings being retained to support a superior ROCE of 8.17% that beats the sector benchmark of 6.56% [E9] and comfortably outpaces the sector median ROCE of 7.1% [E66].

Conceded: quarterly operating margins expanded by +2 percentage points to 10% in Mar 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E22], driving a margin expansion screen signal [E56]. However, dismissing the multi-year margin contraction from 10% down to 9% misses the structural reality that profitability has deteriorated over a three-year horizon [E21]. Characterizing the 52-week range sitting at 0% of its high-low span [E5] as an attractive entry point ignores that a price of ₹ 40.2 [E2] trading directly at its absolute low signals persistent and severe downward market sentiment rather than a temporary washout. Furthermore, attributing the 0.00% dividend yield [E4] to retained earnings powering a superior ROCE of 8.17% [E9] overlooks the company's persistently anaemic returns, evidenced by a low 3-year median return on equity of 6% [E19] and a 4.67% ROE that trails the sector benchmark of 4.86% [E8]. Finally, while the bull cites an 8.17% ROCE beating the sector benchmark of 6.56% [E9], filed statements independently place the company's ROCE at a modest 8.8% [E10] alongside official flags warning of a depressed 6.26% three-year return on equity [E53].
